pr_title: Make the rendering method dropdown also affect mobile if compatible
pr_body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72460.

This prevents visual discrepancies between desktop and mobile platforms after switching rendering methods using this dropdown.

The restart dialog now displays which rendering methods will be used, and the dropdown tooltip also lists caveats related to specific platforms.

I've tested all switching combinations and can confirm it works as expected. Note that `project.godot` will not store default values, so you won't see the `mobile` rendering method being visibly stored in that file for the `.mobile` override (but `gl_compatibility` will).

- This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/73712.

issue_context.title: Can't change rendering method in the Android editor using the dropdown in the top-right corner / Exported mobile project doesn't use specified rendering method
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Version v4.0.rc.custom_build [8c7b98d]

### System information

Galaxy Tab S6 Lite running Android 12

### Issue description

After creating a project on android, attempting to change the renderer from Mobile to Compatibility or the other way around just results in the Godot Splash screen appearing for a few seconds, without the change being applied.

### Steps to reproduce

On Android, create a new Project.
Afterwards attempt to change the renderer.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/60353.

I remember seeing an issue for this already (specifically for the rendering method selection dropdown), but I can't find it right now.

I can confirm this on 4.0.rc3. This is caused by the rendering dropdown not changing the `.mobile` override, so https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72461 fixes this.

As a workaround, change **Rendering Method.mobile** in the Project Settings instead (the `.mobile` is important).

> How would one change "Rendering Method.mobile" ? :)

In the project settings [rendering/renderer/rendering_method.mobile](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-rendering-renderer-rendering-method-mobile)

> With what value, mobile?

If you want to switch to the Compatibility rendering method, use `gl_compatibility` on the `mobile` override but make sure you also change it for the non-overridden setting (so visuals on your PC will match the mobile device).

review_comments:
This will overwrite the setting even if it was intentionally set to forward_plus or gl_compatibility by the user.

I'm not sure the mobile setting should be secretly changed by the engine without the user's knowledge

I feel like we created a pretty complicated situation with the platform overrides for the rendering method. It fully makes sense technically but it's quite complex to understand for users, and for us to update programmatically.

This is especially complex because only some of the choices are valid for mobile and web, so when choosing "Forward+", you're actually only choosing what can be used for desktop, despite the drop down, or the radio buttons on the project manager, showing you a single choice.

Maybe we should design a dedicated dialog for renderer selection, that would replace the dropdown in the editor, so it would let you see the renderer for all target platforms, and have clear visual feedback on what might end up being an invalid or unexpected configuration (e.g. `gl_compatibility` for desktop but `mobile` for mobile).
Yes, that makes sense. Having the little dropdown definitely isn't clear enough anymore.

The dropdown options could be changed to show which option would be used on which platform, e.g. "Forward+ (desktop)/Forward Mobile (mobile)/Compatibility (web)". That said, I don't know if you can display a selected text that is different from the option text (so that the name in the top-right corner isn't too ling).

A dedicated dialog would be ideal, but at the same time, I feel there are only 3 configurations that really make sense from an user perspective:

- Forward+ (desktop)/Forward Mobile (mobile)/Compatibility (web)
- Forward Mobile (desktop)/Forward Mobile (mobile)/Compatibility (web)
- Compatibility (desktop)/Compatibility (mobile)/Compatibility (web)

99% of the time, you want rendering methods to match across platforms as much as possible to ease cross-platform testing.

Coming from this newly-linked issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/7767.

I think the ease of having these three options in a simple, color-coded dropdown is hard to beat.

I quite like your idea of having the dropdown being an 'upper limit,' where mobile maxes-out at Mobile, and web maxes-out at Compatibility. It would give users control and safety.

Alternatively, setting web and mobile to the same value via this dropdown makes complete sense to me. It's a big-hammer (befitting such a prominent button), but I can always split the platforms back to different renderers using the Project Settings, once I've figured out which platforms suit my project.

Future mobile and XR hardware will likely be capable of rendering with Forward+ (at some point), so not placing a soft limit via the menu does provide a measure of future-proofing.

Having said all that, I'd be in favor of either of these two options.

I discussed this with @BastiaanOlij on RocketChat and we both agree that Calinou's last suggestion is a good idea. 

I think leaving the dropdown option text as is, but using the configurations suggested make sense. From a user perspective, they will be setting the desktop mode, but the mobile mode will tag along in a way that makes sense. 

I see two situations where there may still be confusion:
1. The user has set desktop and mobile to Forward+ in the project settings, then tests out mobile or compatibility. Once they return to Forward+, the project setting is incorrect
2. The user wants to test mobile on desktop and compatibility on mobile (I understand this is a useful configuration for games that ship on both PCVR and mobile VR)

To alleviate those issues, I suggest that the popup menu includes a short warning i.e. "this will modify the rendering_method project settings from their current values to: ..." So users are warned that they are changing multiple settings.

I've updated the PR accordingly (check OP for screenshots) :slightly_smiling_face:
